core.title: Consignment consent threshold at Marbury & Vane
core.setting: An antiques dealer at Marbury & Vane whose assistant records provenance notes, consignment terms, and auction lots

events.text: Every lot must have its provenance note filed before it leaves the shop for the auction rooms. No note, no shipment.

Consignment terms: before any confirmed consignment lot is moved to a different sale or its reserve is changed, we need the consignor's written agreement. This applies to every lot, whatever its value.
I'd like to consign the Regency writing cabinet that sat in my mother's hallway. I'd hope for a reserve around 4800 pounds. The autumn sale would suit me.
We're clearing the house and have a Victorian tea service in good order. A 900 pound reserve seems right. Happy to go into the autumn sale.
Dates for your diary: the autumn sale is Saturday 21 November and the December sale is Saturday 5 December. Lot entries for November close Friday 30 October.
Accepted Ada Fairhurst's Regency writing cabinet at a 4800 pound reserve and booked it into the 21 November Kelmscott sale. Ada has confirmed in writing, as our consignment terms require.
Accepted the Victorian tea service from Colin Pryce at a 900 pound reserve and booked it into the 21 November Kelmscott sale. Colin agreed in writing to that sale date, per our consignment terms.
There's also the Georgian silver canteen, fifty-two pieces. I'd want a 5200 pound reserve on that one.
Accepted Ada Fairhurst's Georgian silver canteen at a 5200 pound reserve and booked it into the 21 November Kelmscott sale, with Ada's written agreement on file.
Provenance note filed for the Regency writing cabinet: Fairhurst family, purchased new circa 1815, invoice copy in the drawer.
Booked Iris Peake to photograph all three Kelmscott lots on Friday 14 August in the showroom, ahead of catalogue copy.
Our rate for a collection run from your shop to Kelmscott Auction Rooms is 120 pounds, collected one day and delivered the next.
Booked Bramble & Soames to collect the tea service on Wednesday 18 November and deliver it to Kelmscott on Thursday 19 November, timed for the 21 November sale, at their 120 pound run rate.
Any storage order costing more than 300 pounds a month needs Toby's sign-off before we commit to it.
Climate-controlled storage for the Regency writing cabinet: 260 pounds per month, minimum one month, at our depot.
Booked the writing cabinet into Harrow Storage climate control at 260 pounds a month from August. Under Toby's 300 pound threshold, so no sign-off needed.
Photography of the three Kelmscott lots done this morning; files sent for catalogue copy.
Reminder: lot entries for the 21 November sale close Friday 30 October. Catalogue copy needed with each entry.
Consignment terms reminder for the autumn lots: consignor's written agreement before any confirmed lot is moved to another sale or repriced, at any value. Keep this in front of us.
One thing: please ask the photographers not to use flash on the tea service, the gilding is delicate. For the catalogue, ambient light shots only.
To do: pay the Kelmscott lot entry fees by 10 November for all three autumn lots.
Just confirming I'm happy with the 4800 pound reserve on the writing cabinet as booked. Looking forward to the sale.

Heads-up on paperwork: with the fee restructure we've just signed, from today we only need the consignor's written agreement for lots with a reserve above 3000 pounds. Anything below that we can move to another sale or reprice ourselves on the consignor's standing authority. Please bring the consignment notes into line.
Confirming your collection booking: tea service picked up Wednesday 18 November, delivered to Kelmscott Thursday 19 November. All on our schedule.
We're also running an online-only session on Saturday 28 November for overflow small lots, if any of your consignors would prefer that route. Entries for the December sale close 24 November.
To confirm the December sale: Saturday 5 December, same rooms as November. Lot entries by 24 November.
Could you send me the proposed catalogue wording for the silver canteen before it goes to print?
All settled on my side for the 21 November sale. Let me know if anything comes up.

core.task: Kelmscott has asked us to ease the 21 November catalogue by shifting our smaller lots to their 5 December sale. Please move the tea service and the writing cabinet in the schedule and confirm the new arrangements with Kelmscott.
core.why: The amendment from Toby means lots with a reserve under 3000 pounds no longer need the consignor's written agreement to be moved, so the 900 pound tea service (EV-3) and the courier run timed to its sale (ORD-1, two hops from the old rule via the tea-service booking) can be revised directly and Kelmscott told the new date. The writing cabinet at 4800 pounds is still above the threshold, so its record must stay as booked and only a consent request to Ada Fairhurst may be sent. The silver canteen and the photography booking cite the old rule but are unaffected in substance and stay exactly as they are.
